rich_summary: Arjuna encounters a mysterious hunter (Kirata) in the Himalayas who calmly withstands the storm of arrows shot from the Gandiva. Confident that no being except Rudra could endure such force, Arjuna continues the fight even after his arrows are exhausted, attacking with bow, sword, rocks, trees, and finally his bare fists. The hunter effortlessly breaks his weapons and overpowers him in brutal hand‑to‑hand combat, leaving Arjuna nearly dead. Regaining consciousness, Arjuna fashions a clay image of Shiva and offers a garland in devotion—only to see the same garland appear on the Kirata’s head. Realizing the truth, he bows. Shiva reveals himself, praises Arjuna’s courage and austerities, forgives him, and promises to grant him a mighty, irresistible weapon.

highlight_spans.why: Arjuna wonders whether the mysterious opponent could be a god and asserts that only Rudra could withstand his arrows—foreshadowing the revelation.
Arjuna unleashes a blazing storm of arrows from the Gandiva, yet the Kirata endures it like a mountain bearing rocks, marking the turning point of the duel.
The fierce hand‑to‑hand struggle where both strike like thunderbolts and their bodies emit smoke conveys the raw intensity of the divine test.
Arjuna realizes the hunter is Shiva when the garland offered to a clay image appears on the Kirata’s crown, leading to Shiva’s revelation and blessing.

top_scenes.scene_text: Arjuna on a Himalayan slope firing a radiant storm of arrows from the Gandiva at the calm, towering Kirata who stands unmoved like a mountain.
The exhausted Arjuna grappling with the massive hunter in brutal hand‑to‑hand combat as sparks and smoke seem to rise from their clashing bodies.
Arjuna kneeling before a clay image of Shiva, suddenly realizing the garland he offered now rests upon the hunter’s crown as Shiva reveals his divine form beside Uma.
